isBasedOn.name: Can Reputation Prevent Model Collapse? A Preregistered Test of Reputation-Weighted Data Filtering

abstract: Intelligence models increasingly learn from data that earlier Intelligence models produced, and when that loop repeats the rare cases disappear first. This paper preregisters a test of whether a reputation-weighted validator pool, filtering the training data of a recursive replacement loop, keeps those rare cases alive. The outcomes remain sealed until a replication of the original model-collapse result succeeds.

additionalProperty.value: A positive reading on substrate G needs nine superior labels. For a contrast with paired seed-level standard deviation sd over S seeds, se = sd/ S. Under a normal approximation and a true effect δalt, the label power is ( Φ​ δalt−max(δ, z1−0.05/24 se) se ), z1−0.05/24 ≈ 2. 865, where z1−0.05/24 is the critical value at the most demanding Holm step and Φ is the standard normal distribution function. The design takes the product of the nine single-test powers as the conjunction power. At S = 200 and δalt = 0. 15, the break-even sd for a conjunction power of 0. 80 is about 0. 36, a figure that holds only when the comparator's retention is at most 0. 85. If the ten percent arm's retention exceeds 0.90 in a family, the pool cannot be labeled superior to it there, and no positive reading is possible.
